summary: fsync takes a write through the page cache to a disk on IDE, so that it survives a power cut; the scenario is machine/persist_scenario.c

cases.behavior: a file written and synced on a KRFFS root mounted from a disk on IDE reads back in the next boot of the disk, after the first was cut off

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the copy, run persistprobe write at the debug shell, take its report from the console and end the machine with QMP's quit
boot the same copy again, run persistprobe read at the debug shell, take its report from the console and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: the first boot finds no /persist.txt on the root before it writes
the first boot creates /persist.txt and writes the marker whole
fsync of the file and sync return 0
the first boot runs until QMP's quit ends it, so that no unmount wrote the disk after the probe
the second boot of the same copy opens /persist.txt
the read gives the marker's length
the bytes read are the marker the first boot wrote

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case cuts the machine off between two boots of one disk, whose root the kernel mounts from the disk on IDE
